## Timed setpoints for on/off heating and cooling

HEM now applies the requested two-stage sequence to native thermostatic on/off devices:

| Direction | After native ON is confirmed | Before native OFF |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heating | Wait 30 seconds, then send the device's reported maximum temperature | Send the device's reported minimum temperature, then wait 30 seconds before OFF |
| Cooling | Wait 30 seconds, then send the device's reported minimum temperature | Send the device's reported maximum temperature, then wait 30 seconds before OFF |

The limits come from the original native Home Assistant entity. They are not the room comfort target or HEM's room target limits. The startup wait also covers manual/profile temperature requests, setpoint-only control, temperature ranges, and humidity setpoints.

### Timing and recovery

- The startup wait begins with confirmed/observed native ON, not the request to turn on. A genuine OFF-to-ON event during persistence invalidates an older setpoint request, including when state refreshes coalesce.
- Minimum ON time still precedes the shutdown setpoint. Normal maximum-runtime stops begin preparing 30 seconds early when the configured minimum ON permits it.
- The shutdown wait begins when the reverse-setpoint service call completes. A late or missing temperature acknowledgement does not restart that timer or indefinitely block OFF. Temperature feedback is still recorded separately; it never proves native OFF.
- Once the shutdown target has been dispatched, the device finishes that OFF cycle before any new active setpoint. Renewed demand observes the normal minimum OFF time after native OFF is confirmed.
- A per-device timer requests a normal serialized evaluation at the deadline. It does not issue actuator calls outside the existing controller lock. Unavailable hardware, defrost, identity/ownership changes and genuine manual intervention retain their existing holds.
- Committed shutdown evidence survives Home Assistant restarts. Interrupted calls remain explicitly uncertain, with conservative recovery waits and bounded OFF retries. An explicit successful physical reconciliation can resolve an obsolete device episode without issuing a device command itself.
- Devices without thermostatic heat/cool setpoints retain their own existing OFF behavior. Dedicated upstream switches remain governed by their separate native-OFF verification and cooldown.

### Card

Startup and shutdown waits show their actual remaining seconds, with clear English, Greek and German labels and English fallback. A normal 30-second wait does not ask for repeated manual checks or appear as a device fault. Native mode, measured temperature, reported target and requested target remain distinct. The separated, consistent room readings from Beta 107 are included.

### Verification and update

Automated tests exercise the real native command/persistence/ACK paths with simulated Home Assistant state and service transport: startup boundaries, both heating and cooling extrema, normal cycling and protective stops, delayed feedback, exact dispatch timestamps, restart/uncertain-call recovery, bounded retries, explicit reconciliation and deadline scheduling. The browser tests render the actual card and preserve the inherited regression suite. These checks do not verify a user's physical thermostat.

Update to **v0.6.0b109** in HACS, restart Home Assistant, and hard-refresh the dashboard.
